title: The Role and Fidelity of the Wife
english: After being born, the sequence of living together is necessary, which should be honored as God's law. Those joined to one another are no longer two, but one flesh; so what God has joined, let no man separate (Matthew 19:6). These things were said to the Pharisees then; but now listen, you who easily change markets and wives like garments; who frequently and easily frequent the brothels as if they were festival works; who marry for ease and trade wives; who are easily provoked and immediately write the document of divorce; who leave many widows while still living.

Be persuaded that marriage is cut off only by death and adultery. For it is not like the concubines, where a short number of days disturbs the living together and only hunts pleasure, so it is with those performed according to law and decree; but on the contrary, O man, a single union occurs of both body and soul, just as character is intertwined with character and the flesh is in a certain way bound to the fleshesh.

How then will you cut it off indifferently? How will you easily and without pain withdraw, having taken a share of life, having served for only a few days, the sister and wife? A sister according to the word of formation and creation, for from one cause of the earth and the same matter you came into being; but a wife through the union of the marriage, through the law of marriage.

What then bond will you break, being bound by law and by nature? And how will you set aside the vows which you laid upon the marriage? And who does he think I am to speak to you? Is it perhaps regarding the dowry written here, when with your own hand I mark it in the book while sealing the completed things?
For those are indeed strong and have sufficient security; yet I refer myself to the voice of Adam (Genesis 2:23): 'This is flesh of my flesh and bone of my bones; she shall be called my wife.'

This voice is not preserved as a vain copy, but is a common confession of men, set forth through the one person of this first man for the common multitude of women joining to men by law. And do not marvel if, from those whom another said, another is held accountable. For all things that happened concerning the first-formed in the beginning, these...

A nature of a following kind was produced. If, having taken the book of creation, a wife abandoned her mother and dragged you before the judge, the very same judge and witness, what words would you say? How will you erase your own voice, which you made before God, where the writer became Moses, the servant of God, instead of a mere scribe?

God gave the woman to Adam without fault and without blemish, and for this reason, as a good guardian, He protected the orphan. But now daughters use the rights of the mother strongly against ignorant and faithless men, so that for you, contempt for the wife is impossible from any direction, being bound by the ancient divine laws and the new human ones.

Let the usefulness of the woman for life also restrain you. She is a member, she is a helper; a partner for the enjoyment of life and for the generation of children; a helper in sickness, a consolation in tribulations, a guardian of the hearth, a treasure of possessions; the same when grieving, the same when rejoicing; possessing wealth in common, if it should fail; managing hard poverty, bravely and patiently enduring what is painful through her, toiling in child-rearing because of her dwelling with you.

But if a crisis of circumstances should seize her, she vanishes when baptized; but those considered friends, measuring friendship by the season of prosperity, withdraw in terrible times; slaves flee both the master and the misfortunes together.

Therefore, the wife remains: a member of the part that is sick, a slave to the evils, and the tear that wipes away the healing of the husband; healing the wound if it is struck; following the one being led to prison; and even if one allows her to enter, she shares the pleasure of the confinement; but if even this is forbidden, she remains at the doors of the prison, as a little dog accustomed to her master.

I knew a woman who had cut her hair and put on manly clothing, this flowering garment, so that she would not be separated while the man was fleeing and hiding. She seemed to be a slave, but truly she was a slave to passion; and she lived this life for many years, moving from place to place and from desert to desert. We find such a thing also in the most patient Job.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Virtues of a Wife vs. the Cruelty of Men
english: For everyone left her; even the flatterers fled with the wealth, and friends measured their friendship by the season of prosperity. If they did happen to appear, their presence was a reproach rather than a visit; a burden of misfortune, not a consolation. Therefore, all the bad comforters withdrew from him.

But she, who was once distinguished by her toil, stayed with her husband, leaving aside the filth and pulling out the worms of the wounds. Thus, she was a partner of his life, not a companion of his prosperity; an inseparable friend, not a flatterer of pleasures; leaving behind only all kindness, all most-dear qualities, and all kinship.

Therefore, out of extreme and excessive friendship for a man, and toward the sin of blasphemy, she fell, so that the man might not be punished for a long time, nor see him in unmanageable pains, by saying a blasphemous word toward God, advising [him] and that he might undergo a swift end. For she did not consider her own remaining misfortune, that of widowhood; but she had only one concern, how the man might escape an unlivable life. These things, along with the new trial and the memory of the old, instruct the wedding-insulter.

What then would the one responsible for the accusation say toward these things? And what kind of fair-faced defense of his own ease would he put forward? 'Worthless,' he says, 'and worthy of hatred is the character of the woman, and her tongue is impudent, and her manner is not domestic, and her management is lawless.' Let it be so; let it be granted. I am completely persuaded and I accept, that judges who are not very precise in hearing easily are dragged along by the attacks of the accusers.

But you say: 'While leading the beginning, did you not know that you were connecting with a human? And having heard of a human, does one not immediately see a small sin following? For God's alone is the ungraspable. Do you not yourself sin? And do you not cause grief to the woman by your manner? And are you innocent of all wrongdoing and do you keep the institution of living together without corruption?'

O how much chance of rebuke your wife brought! And how many ready insults and indecent words she endured! And how many of your faults are kept silent, because the woman did not publish them! She endured you even while you were becoming angry and your spirit was boiling; and the free and equal [one] was silenced.

She was like a slave from a market. She did not reproach you for not providing the necessities for the conduct of life due to poverty or stinginess. Nor did she ever reject you after coming from a banquet, having drunk wine and being out of her mind because she hated drunkenness; rather, she received you with human sympathy, and she led you, who were punishing yourself, and she treated the head with the vapors of the wine being poured out. And she alone, sympathizing, led you to the marriage bed, while the servants were laughing and mocking the excess from the drunkenness.

But you, bypassing the amphorae, sing songs against the woman on cold pretexts, so that you might prepare sympathy for yourself for the imminent division. The mind of such men is hard, beastly and unmerciful, having a birth from oak or stone, according to what is said. For they are cut off indifferently, erasing the memory of all at once.

But who, instead of healing a sick limb, cuts it off, and this not having considered a dangerous disease, but having much hope for an easy cure? A blister occurred on the hand, let us treat it carefully; an inflammation pursued the foot, let us settle the irritation with medicine. And if, being present, we had attended to the physicians' inspection regarding the incision and the iron, and had occupied ourselves with each of those who were suffering, we would not have lost even a small amount of life's time, but would have amputated ourselves for all the limbs.

But not so, O men; let there be some memory of the punishments; let the healings of women make you ashamed. However much you may be provoked, if you withstand the pangs of a single birth against the reproaches, you will find the situation of those who suffer to be conquered.

Let the calculation be referred to the middle, and let the good things be included in the goodwill: the healing of diseases, the sharing of misfortunes, the tears presented to some on behalf of a husband, the leaving of those she gave birth to and the parental table to follow a stranger, the selling of something of her own so that she might drive away the insolence and trouble of the husband. Let all these things instruct toward a disposition and let them become a bond of affection, such as a more modest house awakening and holding together the easily slipping soul. But let mercy prevail, and habit, and living together for a long time, let it not be struck by...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Bond of Marriage and the Call to Sobriety
english: It is irrational of animals to be held together without passion. For I saw with passion a bellowing ox, because having wandered from its companions it remained stuck, and a sheep being thrown into a pit and running through the mountains until it could reunite with the flock from which it was separated while grazing. And a goat, experiencing this same thing, even if it runs through many herds of kids, does not stand still until it finds its usual place and its own sharp-edged way.

Therefore, let us not be found more passionless toward friendship than the irrational ones who are rational, nor let us judge the marriage of a companion to be less honorable because of having become friendly in a short time through a small pretext. You see how even on the high road, men having mixed with one another, having gone under the same roof of a building or having shaded themselves at midday in a tree embracing them in the season of summer, make the encounter an occasion for genuine disposition; and even if they come to the road that divides, they do not depart from one another passionlessly, but they stand and weep, looking intently at one another, and each gives tokens of memory to carry; and having advanced a little, they turn back again and call out, and one prays for the other the spiritual things; and does a little time thus sharpen the friendship so acutely, that it becomes unchangeable to them and their departure is established?

But you, toward the one who is a sharer of life, act so contemptuously, as toward a vessel fallen or a cheap garment forgotten on a journey or a rag of the Melitians departing a house? And where is the disposition formed in the beginning? Where is the rest upon the one bed, the joining of the law, the strength of much and long habit, which is even transformed into nature and has a reason, and experience has shown? Having cut off everything more easily than Samson cut the cords of the Philistines (Judges 16).

Even if he is sober and a guardian of his disposition, he does not easily forget the life of the marriage even after it has departed, but he warms the children as a common deposit of the mother and of nature, and in them he seems to see the one who has gone. For one preserves the likeness of the mother's voice, another is drawn to much of the character, another is formed in the state of the character toward the one who bore him; and thus the father [preserves] many.

Having the living and manifest image of the marriage as an immortal pattern, he imagines the cohabitation toward it and for this reason does not conceive any unseemly thought. Not today, having entered the tomb, after a little time, does he prepare wedding feasts; nor does he hasten to a wedding dance again after the weeping and the groans; nor does he mix the black and mourning garment into a bridal attire; nor does he introduce a second marriage into the warm bed of the one who has departed; nor does he give the heavy name to the children.

He imitates the irrational and natural dignity of the birds. For they say that even that bird, having been separated from its mate, loves the widowship continuously and stands in opposition to the dove, making it easy toward polygamy.

Until this, let the man be cast heavily with accusations, and let the insults of ignorance sting him more densely with veils. If, however, an accusation of adultery is brought forward and such is provided as the defense for the separation, I will immediately shift my sympathy to the wronged one, and having prepared the argument against the adulteress, I will stand as a good ally to the man instead of an enemy, praising the one who fled the aggressor, the one who broke the bond to which he was bound with a shield or an echidna.

For by this, the Creator of all gives forgiveness first, as it is just for one who is suffering and rightly driving away the sickness of the house and the hearth. For marriage consists of these two: disposition and child-rearing, neither of which is saved after adultery. For the disposition is not one that turns away from another of goodwill; and child-rearing is lost when the children are poured out.

But regarding those leading toward this, the sin is stated in another hypothesis proportionately. Let both sides practice sobriety, the unbreakable bond of marriages. For where this is honored, there must always be both peace and longing, without the soul desiring any common and illegitimate passion, casting out the lawful and just affection.
This law of sobriety was established by God not for women only, but also for men. And those paying attention to the law-makers of this life are not without shame.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
